title: Admit another host's supersede or cancel of a shared task through task-sync import instead of refusing it as unsupported fields
outcome: Admit another host's supersede or cancel of a shared task through task-sync import instead of refusing it as unsupported fields
acceptance: When one host supersedes a shared task (`update supersede` with a replacement and reason) and exports it, an ordinary task-sync import on another enrolled host applies the supersession: the task becomes superseded by the same replacement with the same disposal reason, through the existing disposal transition, instead of refusing the task with unsupported_fields lifecycle, superseded_by, disposal_reason
The same holds for a cancellation with a disposal reason

A disposition the receiving host cannot apply (for example the replacement is absent, or the task has engaged local execution) is held or refused by name with a remedy that the next step accepts, never applied partially

A two-store CLI test supersedes a shared task on one host and observes the other host's ordinary import apply it, and the docs (task-planning-text.md 'Edits on an enrolled destination') describe the admitted disposition
disposal_reason: Duplicate: w-aedc1cb982d2 already tracks the import refusing a Changed delta whose lifecycle, superseded_by or disposal_reason differ, with a fix in progress; this case (w-8448 on TermAl's WinB) is recorded there as its second occurrence
